ratings.reason: The new union semantics is fully documented in the schema, matched by the code, and tested for both the unset and set cases, so no surface is misleading; the residual complaint is a design-flexibility loss (no opt-in narrowing), not a defect a reader would be misled by.

The new docstring states the opposite of what the code does on name collisions -- a clean contradiction between surfaces -- though today's behavior matches base and no live collision exists, so the wrong belief is real but not yet acted on.

The growths use the ratchet's own documented escape (re-baselining an already-over-cap unit), which the scan's docstring names as a known, accepted trade-off and which the new RAISED-row listing already surfaces for review, so this is the design working as stated rather than a hidden defect.

Exit 0 on a failed ROUND.toml record contradicts the project's own exit-code contract and the identical-class ConfigWrittenError handling in the same diff, but the trigger (the tool composing invalid ROUND.toml) is itself an abnormal precondition, not something normal use reaches on its own.

The updated policy text promises mid-round script replacement only when frozen scripts cannot run, but the code checks nothing but reason length, so any sufficiently long string defeats the frozen-mid-round guarantee central to this tool -- a wrong belief about the API reachable by ordinary use, compounded by two concrete paths where the replacement leaves no record at all.

The relaxations are unscoped: any ROUND.toml (not just abandoned imports) can now carry a blank config_sha undetected by schema validation even when closed, and `import --empty` now silently succeeds and writes round data in a directory with no consumer config or git repo where it used to refuse -- both are ordinary-use misfires, not edge cases, and both erode the round record's integrity guarantees.

record_build! silently accepts builds from prepare/pass open with no porcelain check while pass_open's own reuse logic treats a dirty tree as meaningless, widening two new implicit, unguarded entry points into a real (if pre-existing) hole where close can be satisfied by a stale/discarded build.

the tool-id regex narrowing is undisclosed by the adjacent comment but the corpus impact is only 3 lines today, and the finding itself concedes the tightening is a defensible, plausibly-intentional design choice, not a mischaracterization with material consequence.

reintroduces exactly the stale-count risk the base design deliberately avoided, and backs it with a categorical 'every count is dated' claim that the same document's own undated counts (schemas; PF/IT/SS surfaces) directly falsify.

the pre-fix PINNED/MANAGED sentence about managed.json is left verbatim in two live user-facing CLI refusal strings and an ARCHITECTURE narrative a reader hits before the corrected §7.3 row, a direct contradiction between surfaces a user plausibly encounters at the terminal.

install.md now explicitly points to the glossary as the authoritative binding of 'consumer' in the very edit that broadens the definition, but the glossary it cites still states the narrower, now-contradicted definition — a self-created contradiction between cross-referenced surfaces.

a stale Args-comment/dead-parameter pattern left unswept in one internal workflow script's comment while two siblings were corrected — a secondary, developer-facing surface with no functional effect since no caller ever passed batch in any version.

Verified: RULES.toml's RULE.INST.CARRY statement now has two sentences distinguishing a round-close refusal (carrying a finding already at CARRY_LIMIT) from the release refusal, but ARCHITECTURE.md's §12.A rule-id table row — the authoritative design record's dedicated mirror of RULES.toml, kept in lockstep for the sibling rule touched in the same diff — still carries only the old, single-sentence release-only wording, so a reader of that table would form the wrong belief that only release (not close) is blocked by a carry-limit finding.
